text:
maria: Quick check — I'm rolling a change to move our k8s secrets from in-cluster AES to envelope encryption using KMS + secrets-store.csi. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421. Can someone skim the Terraform + Helm bits? Concern: rotation behavior for existing secrets and whether pods will see updates.

jon: :eyes: I can take a look. Are you mounting plaintext via CSI or syncing to native k8s Secret objects?

maria: Syncing to k8s Secrets (sync enabled). Terraform adds an aws_kms_key + Helm values for the CSI driver. Example TF snippet in the PR: ```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "dek" {
  description = "k8s envelope DEK"
  deletion_window_in_days = 7
}
```
And simplified Helm values I pushed: ```yaml
secretsStore:
  provider: aws
  sync:
    enabled: true
    path: /var/run/secrets-store
  kmsKeyAlias: "alias/infra-secrets"
```

sam: Two gotchas to watch: 1) sync creates/upserts k8s Secrets—ensure the CSI controller/service account has `create`/`update` perms for secrets in target namespaces. 2) Rotation: KMS key rotation doesn't automatically trigger CSI to re-sync; you'll need a rewrap or reapply flow to force a refresh.

kevin: +1. If we want zero-downtime rotation: create a new KMS key, rewrap DEKs (or create new DEKs wrapped by new KEK), then update the cluster encryption config. Without that, old secret blobs remain wrapped by the old key and pods won't pick up changes. Consider a small `null_resource` in TF to run a rewrap job or a Kubernetes Job that re-seeds secrets.

maria: Good catch. I added a `null_resource.rewrap` placeholder to the TF and a script: ```bash
./scripts/rotate-encryption-key.sh --cluster prod --new-key alias/infra-secrets-v2
```
Plan: create new key, rewrap secrets in S3 backing store, update helm release values, then `kubectl rollout restart` on apps that mount those secrets.

jon: Can you paste the CI job name so we can gate this? Also add a dry-run mode to the script.

maria: CI job is `infra/secret-migration`. I added `--dry-run` in the script and a `staging` canary flow in the PR. I also added a short checklist in the PR description with validation commands, e.g., `kubectl get secrets -n redwood -o yaml | grep metadata.name`. Link again: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5421 :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: checks passed for PR #5421 — terraform fmt, helm lint, unit tests.

sam: Small nit: in Helm values make sure the key is `secretsStore.sync.enabled: true` and not `sync: enabled: true` at the wrong indentation, otherwise helm-lint complains. Also set `secretsStore.sync.path` explicitly to avoid secret name collisions across namespaces.

kevin: Also add an alerting flag in values so Console picks up failures: `observability.alerts.secret_sync_failure: true`. If the CSI sync fails we should page infra oncall.

maria: Thanks all — I'll run the staging canary tonight. Will @kevin ping when we're ready for prod maintenance window. Any other blockers?

jon: None from me, +1 for dry-run and canary.

sam: :thumbsup: make sure to document rollback steps in the PR.

maria: Will do. Thanks!
